thread:
Hana: heads up — canary perf dashboard just spiked p99 on the hosted path after the release (0.7.3). latency up ~35%.
Mike: saw that. which route is noisy? any model change? :thinking_face:
Hana: it's mostly the streaming/text-generate route hitting kernel-selector + KV prefetch. not a model change in the release, more runtime.
Ashley: CI also flagged a regression earlier in the run: perf/baseline/throughput_test failed p95 threshold on linux-kvm. CI-Bot: [perf/regression] build 7421 exceeded p95 by 28% (compare base: 0.12s -> 0.153s)
Hana: exact symptoms: higher per-token latency when KV cache hits are present, and kernel selector seems to choose the slower attention kernel on short seqs. suspect interaction between KV prefetch and kernel heuristic changes merged in PR #6142.
Oliver: can you paste the failing perf log snippet?
Hana: sure:

```
serve_worker.py: token_emit p50=0.007 p95=0.153 p99=0.344
kv_cache: hit_rate=0.82 prefetch=true prefetch_size=32
kernel_selector: chosen=attention_v2 fallback=attention_v1
profile: cpu_ms=12 gpu_ms=10 gpu_kernel=matmul_pack
```

Ashley: interesting that chosen kernel is attention_v2 — we changed heuristic thresholds in commit 7e2f4c2 (heuristic: prefer v2 when seq <= 32). That commit also added async prefetch for KV in the same PR (7e2f4c2 + 9c3a1b7 merged together).
Mike: OK we need to bisect the merge window. Can someone run a quick git-bisect across the merge? I can do a binary search on the runtime repo but want to coordinate so others don't duplicate.
Hana: proposing range: base tag 0.7.2 -> head 0.7.3. suspect commit list: 7e2f4c2, 9c3a1b7, d8f9a11 (batching tweak), c4a8b33 (kv eviction). But the suspect is likely the async prefetch change (9c3a1b7) interacting with kernel thresholds.
Leah: I can kick off a local reproducible micro-bench on my workstation (A100) — need the exact perf harness commands.
Hana: repro steps I used (short):

```
# checkout runtime @ 0.7.3
./scripts/setup_dev_env.sh
# run synthetic perf harness (single-worker) with kv-hit profile
PYTHONPATH=. python perf/harness.py --scenario streaming --seq-len 16 --kv-hit-rate 0.85 --workers 1 --iterations 500
```

Hana: with that I see p95 regression. On 0.7.2 it reports p95=0.11s, on 0.7.3 p95=0.153s.
Oliver: I'll run a quick git bisect. If we automate harness, we can mark good/bad by p95 threshold. I have a script to return exit code based on p95.
Mike: please share script, Oliver.
Oliver: paste:

```
# bisect-check.sh
python perf/harness.py --scenario streaming --seq-len 16 --kv-hit-rate 0.85 --workers 1 --iterations 250 --json > /tmp/perf.json
p95=$(jq .p95 /tmp/perf.json)
python - <<PY
import sys
if float(sys.argv[1]) < 0.13:
    sys.exit(0)  # good
else:
    sys.exit(1)  # bad
PY $p95
```

Hana: note that noise is non-trivial — run multiple iterations or increase iterations to 500 for reliability.
Leah: running now on my box. will run full 500.
CI-Bot: queued perf job #7435 (range 0.7.2..0.7.3) - will run automated bisect with harness, expect 30-45m.
Ashley: while bisect runs, quick profiling question: does anyone have a flamegraph showing attention_v2 hot paths? I want to see if async prefetch introduces scheduling jitter.
Mike: I ran pprof on a short run earlier — async prefetch spawns a background task which locks the KV store then schedules a cudaMemcpy that blocks the stream until complete — could explain increased tail latency.
Oliver: update: git bisect has narrowed to the merge commit that brought together 7e2f4c2 + 9c3a1b7. Suspect binary interaction rather than single commit.
Hana: yeah that matches our theory. If bisect can't separate, we should try reverting async prefetch patch alone and measure.
Leah: local results: 0.7.2 p95=0.109, 0.7.3 p95=0.154, revert 9c3a1b7 p95=0.112. Reverting only async prefetch makes perf go back to baseline on my A100 run.
Mike: excellent reproduction. Can you double-check with kernel selection forced? e.g., force attention_v1 and v2 to compare.
Leah: forcing attention_v1 on 0.7.3 reduces p95 to 0.114. forcing v2 yields 0.148. So both kernel choice and prefetch interact.
Ashley: conclusion: async prefetch change causes blocking behavior that penalizes attention_v2 relative to v1; and the new heuristic prefers v2 for short seqs — double-hit.
Hana: operationally: hold rollout for 0.7.3 canary and revert async prefetch (9c3a1b7) as hotfix. We'll also open a follow-up to adjust kernel heuristic or make prefetch non-blocking on that path.
SRE-Bot: incident created INC-2026: canary perf regression. Priority P2. Assigned to Hana, Mike.
Mike: I'll prepare the revert PR for async prefetch and land as 0.7.3-hotfix/async-prefetch-revert. Ashley — can you own the follow-up to make prefetch truly non-blocking and add a unit test for kernel heuristic interaction?
Ashley: on it. I'll file an RFC and attach perf benchmarks. Also will add an integration perf test in CI gating to catch similar regressions.
Hana: thanks team. Leah/Oliver — can you both run the hotfix build in staging and post results here? If staging looks good we can proceed with rollback.
Leah: staging build (hotfix) p95=0.113, matches baseline. posting screenshots to #eng-runtime-dashboard.
Oliver: hotfix verified on my local and staging. will hold canary and coordinate release rollback.
Mike: final note — add a bisect label to PRs that touch both kernel selector and KV to avoid future joint-merge surprises.
Hana: agreed. closing loop after rollback completes. :thumbsup:
